ZONES.name: Open parking
ZONES.sub: Ground level · full sun · the real orchard
ZONES.d: Better than the terrace for anything heavy. Ground runs several degrees cooler at night than a concrete roof, there is less wind shear, water is at hand, and you never carry a 24-inch bag up four flights.
ZONES.foot: Build the 50% shade frame with foggers here. This is where the money goes.

ZONES.name: Terrace
ZONES.sub: 4th floor · maximum light · hot and windy
ZONES.d: Most light on the site and the harshest conditions. Reserve it for plants that want heat and tolerate wind, and solve the root-zone problem before anything goes up.
ZONES.foot: Raise everything on pallets, double-pot, mulch two inches, pale bags only. Run a tap up here — in May a watering job that needs carrying does not get done.

ZONES.name: South balcony, closed
ZONES.sub: Winter sun trap · summer shade house
ZONES.d: The best growing space you have, for a reason worth understanding: at this latitude the June sun passes almost overhead, so an overhang shades a south balcony all summer. In December the sun sits low in the south and floods it.
has: Strawberry · fig, once you have one
ZONES.foot: Two fixes. Closed means still air — run a fan or open it daily or spider mites arrive within a month. And no wind means no pollination: flick every open flower each morning.

ZONES.name: First-floor shade
ZONES.d: Permanent home for everything that genuinely prefers shade, plus the seedling bench. Your grafted chilli lives here until October.
has: Finger lime · kaffir lime · curry leaf
Seedling nursery — every tray starts here
ZONES.foot: Anything bought for shade stays in shade. Moving it out is how you lose it.

ZONES.name: Closed parking
ZONES.d: The piece that was missing. Too dark to grow anything long-term, perfect for everything else.
has: Acclimation ward — every new arrival, 7–10 days
Hospital — scorched or freshly repotted plants
Propagation bench — mulberry and fig cuttings
Heatwave refuge, a few days only
ZONES.foot: This is why the eight plants are alive. Never skip it, however healthy the stock looks.

ACCLIM.d: Deep shade, no direct sun. Water lightly. Do not repot.
Bright, indirect. Watch for wilting at midday.
First real sun, filtered. Roughly a week.
Morning sun first, afternoon sun last.
